basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A forward-looking plan and authorization of resources, distinct from the ledger of actual transactions.
Passes through proposal, review and authorization; each version keeps its status.
Commitments and actuals are referenced for availability and variance, not owned.
Differs from a forecast, which estimates outcomes without granting authority to spend.

may: Draft budget proposals and line estimates with stated assumptions.
Report availability, variances and forecasts against the authorized budget.
Flag commitments that would exceed ceilings.
mustNot: Authorize, reallocate or amend a budget.
Commit funds beyond the available balance.
Change an authorized version instead of recording an amendment.
Publish draft public budgets before the authorized release.
requiresHuman: Transfers between lines beyond delegated limits.
Cuts affecting staff or public services.

considerations: Budget choices decide who receives services and who bears cuts.
Public budgets carry duties of transparency towards citizens.
Hidden assumptions can make a budget look balanced when it is not.
affectedParties: Staff and programmes funded by the budget
Citizens or customers who rely on funded services

items: A budget has an owner, a period, a boundary, a status such as proposed or authorized, and lines by classification.
It is confused with a forecast, a financial statement and a cost estimate.
Overspending through commitments not checked against availability.
Misleading reports from mixing versions or bases.
Service cuts caused by planning errors.
